executive_assessment.text: Southern drought and service vulnerabilities differ from urban flood pressures in Luanda and historical Benguela sites. Older water-point and disaster figures retain their distinct dates and denominators.

The UN reports a Namibe dam-access clash amid prolonged drought in August 2025. This is a bounded local incident, not an estimated national climate effect; capacity and outlook evidence remain separately dated.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025-11-28 reports: UNOCA reports 17 August clashes between two unnamed communities in Namibe over dam access amid prolonged drought; 12–20 people were killed and thousands displaced.
Source dated 2025-09 reports: NDC links drainage and erosion deficits to flood and life risks in urban Luanda.
Source dated 2025-09 reports: NDC reports over one million people affected in Huíla, Namibe and Cunene during 2015–16 drought, with $286m damage and about $437m losses.
Source dated 2025-09 reports: These wetlands and peatlands support rural water and livelihoods but face fire and land-use pressure.

Source dated 2024-12 reports: In drought-affected Huíla and Cunene, UNICEF reports measles vaccination for 11,587 at-risk children and maternal or child health services for 251,559 women and children.
Source dated 2015-09-10 reports: In August 2015, Angola's Civil Protection Commission and UNDP trained 43 national and provincial officials in Luanda on needs assessment and resilient recovery.

Source dated 2015-09-10 reports: After Benguela floods, a CNPC–UNDP exercise assessed recovery needs in Lobito, Catumbela and Cabrais, including housing, health, education, livelihoods and agriculture.

Source dated 2015-09-10 reports: The report cites OCHA estimates that 2013–14 drought affected 1.8 million people in Cunene, Namibe, parts of Benguela and Huíla; about 700,000 faced food-insecurity risk.
Source dated 2026-06 reports: 2025/26 rains were delayed and dry, with below-average harvests and crop failures at Oncócua, Cunene.
Source dated 2026-06 reports: Some isolated herders in Cunene, Namibe and Cuando Cubango with prior-drought herd losses and few alternatives are assessed as likely IPC Phase 3.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 16 of 17 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No pre-existing AGO country dossier was present under countries/ in this worktree; this is a new-country Phase 2 extraction.
The UN Secretary-General report explicitly relates the Namibe clash to dam access amid prolonged drought, but it does not establish causality independently or identify the communities.
No opened source connected conflict or insecurity to weaker climate adaptation, climate-service delivery or disaster response; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.

The World Bank risk report PDF exceeded the reader size limit, the UNDRR full profile was unavailable beyond landing-page metadata, and the 2026 OHRLLS PDF returned HTTP 403; snippets and metadata were not used for claims.
The NDC uses older southern-province groupings for some historic statistics despite Angola's 2025 administrative reorganization; those aggregate figures are not mapped to new province boundaries.
FEWS NET's outlook is based on information through 30 June 2026 and its projected food-security outcomes are not observed results.

The August 2025 Namibe incident is a source-reported water-access clash under drought. The report does not identify communities, isolate climate causation or provide a current provincial violence trend.
Broad regional humanitarian-access constraints in the UN report are not assigned specifically to Angola's adaptation services.
Historical province labels and drought statistics are preserved without remapping them onto reorganized administrative boundaries.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
